prompt: Pull the Maven coordinates out of a pom.xml text by hand, with plain String searching. Complete PomCoordinateReader, then run the tests.
explanation: indexOf finds the opening tag, and a second indexOf starting just past it finds the closing tag, so substring between them is the element text. Searching from the front is what makes the project's own coordinates win over the ones buried in <dependency> blocks further down. Guarding both indexOf results against -1 is what turns a missing or unclosed tag into "" instead of a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, and trim() removes the whitespace XML allows around values.
hints: Build the two strings you are looking for first: "<" + tag + ">" and "</" + tag + ">".
Pass the index just after the opening tag as the second argument to indexOf so the closing tag is found after it, not before.
Check both indexOf results for -1 before calling substring, and call .trim() on the text you extract.
